description: Liveness probe — no data, no auth.
Static dashboard UI — no live data of its own.

Sets the dashboard operator password for the first time (only while none is set); admin gateway key required. The password is stored only as an Argon2id hash in the data dir; no default password exists.
Operator login with the dashboard password; on success sets an HttpOnly session cookie (12h). Failed attempts are throttled per peer (5 failures → 60s lockout).
Invalidates the dashboard session cookie; 401 when the caller has neither a session nor a gateway key.
Changes the dashboard operator password; requires a valid session plus the current password, or an admin gateway key. All sessions are invalidated.
Live provider facts (verification, wire, health) — no keys, no base URLs.
Live overview KPIs + traffic buckets from the ledger/recorder — counts and totals only, no message content.
Live model catalog from the registry + per-model request counts — no keys, no base URLs.
Last committed catalog freshness audit vs live models.dev (audit date + drift counts) — public catalog facts only, no keys, no operator-configured providers.
Last recorded `release verify` run (verified tag, archive/SBOM counts, bundle status) — the committed snapshot proof only, never a live re-run or an invented pass.

Re-probes every provider's model list live and returns one result per provider (ok / failed / skipped, with model counts and reasons); a failed provider keeps its last known list. Local-operator dashboard action on the localhost-bound server — carries no secrets.
Recent request attempts from the ledger (provider, model, tokens, cost, latency, outcome) — no message content.
Live spend/token roll-up from the ledger — totals only, no keys, no message content.
Gateway-key facts from the config (name, scopes, budget, created) — masked values only, never a raw key or hash.
Live auto-router classification for a typed prompt — no provider is called.
Last real auto/* routing decision, or an honest empty state.
Feedback-learned routing weights: per-tier signal tallies + nudges + recent signals — counts only, no prompts, no answers, no message content.
Records one accept/edit/discard/regenerate signal against a served routing decision id (decision id + signal only; no content). Local-operator dashboard action on the localhost-bound server.

Learned auto-router status: off / learning / active, evidence count, held-out calibration error + log-loss, per-tier sample counts — counts only, no prompts, no answers, no message content, never a fake accuracy.
Intent-tier mappings (fast / balanced / best) to their operator-defined (model, effort) pairs — model names and effort levels only, no keys, no base URLs, no message content.

Sets one intent tier's (model, effort) mapping at runtime (tier, model and effort names only). Local-operator dashboard action on the localhost-bound server — carries no secrets; applies at runtime only, never to the config file.

Metadata-only learning suggestions: pending routing suggestions with their real evidence counts, per-(task, model) latency/success stats and the applied-change log — counts and model names only, no prompts, no answers, no message content.

Approves (applies) or reverts one routing suggestion by id — an explicit operator action recorded in the applied-change log. Local-operator dashboard action on the localhost-bound server — carries no secrets; applies at runtime only, never to the config file.

Auto Code mode evidence: per-model recorded coding-task outcomes (attempts, solved credit, measured solve rate or the documented neutral default) — counts only, no prompts, no answers, no message content.
Single-flight counters only — no keys, no message content.
Reasoning replay counters (captures, restores, hits, misses, evictions) — counts only, never reasoning content, no keys, no message content.

Live Responses feed: recent response ids with model, status, previous id (the continuation chain), serving provider and creation time, plus store counts — identifiers and counts only, never input or output text.

Responses tree: roots with their branches nested (parent → children, from the ledger tree, or the in-memory store when no ledger is wired) — identifiers and counts only, never input or output text; an empty forest is roots [] with total 0.
Adaptive limiter state + TFO probe — no keys, no base URLs.
Warm HTTP/2 pool state per (provider, key) + Little's Law sizing — counters and key fingerprints only, no keys, no base URLs.
Guard-tier table + live guard status — no keys, no secrets.

Audit feed: guard-denial counts (live counters), key-lifecycle events, management POSTs, and the MCP tool-call audit join — counts + redacted identifiers only, no prompts, no keys, no message content. Management auth (admin scope) required.
MCP tool list + live provider/model counts — no keys, no base URLs.
MCP tool-call audit (inputs SHA-256-hashed, outputs truncated to 200 chars — no raw arguments), paginated, newest first. Entries are redacted as stored, so the feed cannot leak a secret.
MCP remote-transport toggles + live session counts — flags and counts only, no keys, no message content.
Enables/disables one MCP remote transport (sse/streamable). Local-operator dashboard action on the localhost-bound server — carries no secrets; the transports themselves are served by M9.2.
MCP SSE transport: opens the server-to-client event stream (first event is the endpoint carrying the session id). Gateway-key auth; the mcp: scopes on the key govern tool calls inside.
MCP SSE transport: sends one JSON-RPC message for a session opened by GET; answers 202, the response arriving on the stream. Gateway-key auth; the mcp: scopes on the key govern tool calls inside.
MCP Streamable HTTP transport: one JSON-RPC message per POST; an initialize opens a session (Mcp-Session-Id header). Gateway-key auth; the mcp: scopes on the key govern tool calls inside.
MCP Streamable HTTP transport: opens the server-to-client stream for a session (closing it does not terminate the session). Gateway-key auth; the mcp: scopes on the key govern tool calls inside.
MCP Streamable HTTP transport: terminates one session (204; unknown or foreign ids are 404). Gateway-key auth; the mcp: scopes on the key govern tool calls inside.
Live guardrail state (blocking config, redaction counts, recent redacted events) — no prompts, no keys.
Replaces the guardrail blocking config (toggles only; log redaction is always on and not toggleable). Local-operator dashboard action on the localhost-bound server — carries no secrets.
Live plugin registry: registered plugins, hook points, per-hook call/error/denial/panic counts, recent response shapes — counts only, no prompts, no keys, no response content.
Honest verification status: what is proven in this VM vs what still needs CI on the first tag, a live browser, a second host, or a real Docker host — statuses only, no keys, no secrets.
Live routing strategies (global strategy, per-chain overrides, deadline budget, last live strategy) — no keys, no base URLs, no message content.
Replaces the global routing strategy and/or per-chain strategy overrides (strategy names only). Local-operator dashboard action on the localhost-bound server — carries no secrets.
Live cooldown mode (global + per-chain overrides) + currently cooling/demoted targets with remaining seconds — mode names and counters only, no keys, no base URLs, no message content.
Replaces the global cooldown mode and/or per-chain cooldown-mode overrides (mode names only: hard / soft-demote). Local-operator dashboard action on the localhost-bound server — carries no secrets.

Operator-defined routing groups (routing.groups) with live member health — group names, member provider IDs, enabled flags, breaker state and real attempt counters only, no keys, no base URLs, no message content.
Stream-lifetime cap the engine enforces (effective cap + how many streams it has terminated since this process started) — a duration and a count only, no keys, no message content.
Per-key rolling 5-hour USD budgets from the ledger (spent/limit, window, unknown spend) — key ids and names only, never a raw key or hash.
Sets or deletes one key's rolling 5-hour USD budget (key id, limit, unpriced policy only). Local-operator dashboard action on the localhost-bound server — carries no secrets.
Fair-share quota pools from the ledger (dimensions with live pool-wide consumption, member allocations) — pool ids, key ids and counts only, never a raw key or hash.
Creates, replaces or deletes one fair-share quota pool (dimensions, allocations, saturation threshold). Local-operator dashboard action on the localhost-bound server — carries no secrets.
Quota schedules from the ledger (time windows, keep-free reserves, per-window budgets, live verdict) — pool and schedule ids only, never a raw key or hash.
Creates, replaces or deletes one quota schedule (allow/block window, reserves, budget). Local-operator dashboard action on the localhost-bound server — carries no secrets.
Internal scoped budgets from the ledger (scope, period, limit type, live usage and decision) — budget ids only, never a raw key or hash.
Creates, replaces or deletes one internal budget (scope, period, limit type, value, warning threshold). Local-operator dashboard action on the localhost-bound server — carries no secrets.
Team cost centers from the ledger (members, budget window, list + metered cost) — team and key ids only, never a raw key or hash.
Creates, replaces or deletes one team cost center (name, budget, duration, status). Local-operator dashboard action on the localhost-bound server — carries no secrets.
Assigns a gateway key to a team, or unassigns it. Local-operator dashboard action on the localhost-bound server — carries no secrets.
Per-request USD budget outcomes since server start (refusals pre-send / mid-chain, overages, recent events) — counts and costs only, no keys, no base URLs, no message content.

Route trace of the most recently finished request: every attempt in order with outcome + error-taxonomy fallback reason (model_not_found, rate_limited, request_invalid, ...) — redacted error strings only, no keys, no base URLs, no message content.

Context-window fit-check decision of the most recently finished request that reached the pre-call fit gate: local prompt estimate, response reserve, required tokens, per-model fit verdicts, and which chain served it (primary / context_fallback / none) — token counts and model names only, no keys, no base URLs, no message content.
Operator-configured per-(provider, model) prices (USD per 1M tokens) from the config file and/or local price file — unknown prices reported as unknown, never $0.

Last measured Geekflare-style bench run from the data dir's benchmark.json (scripts/bench-geekflare.sh output) with per-metric target verdicts — measured values only; recorded=false when no run exists.

Every recorded Geekflare-style bench run (benchmark-*.json in CODVIAN_BENCH_HISTORY_DIR, oldest first) with kind, clean flag, verdict and passes — recorded files only, never invented; unreadable or corrupt files are listed as skipped, not shown as data.

Live memory of this router process (Go heap from runtime.MemStats, RSS, goroutines, in-flight requests, GC counters) + ?profile=heap / ?profile=goroutine binary pprof snapshots — live values only, nothing estimated.
Headless-mode status + the exact terminal commands for serve --headless, init --wizard and run <cli> --model — no keys, no secrets.

Live local-capability readiness: every gateway-provided local capability with its ready state and the Retry-After a client should honour while it is not ready — capability names and states only, no keys, no base URLs.

Last measured SSE token-delivery run from the data dir's streaming.json (scripts/bench-sse.sh output): median/p99 before (batching off) and after (batching on) at each mock cadence — measured values only, no target verdict; recorded=false when no run exists.

OpenAPI spec for the management surface, generated live from this route table. Every operation carries x-loopback-only / x-always-protected / x-spawn-capable extensions matching its tier — the consistency check is TestOpenAPIConsistency.
Live provider feed — no keys, no base URLs.

Adds a provider: tests the supplied key live against the upstream, encrypts and persists it, and adds it to the live registry with no restart. Auth always required — an unauthenticated add could redirect future LLM traffic to an attacker-chosen base URL.

Removes a provider: deletes it from the live registry and the config file, drops its live engine client, unregisters its models from the auto-router tiers (only models no remaining provider serves), and prunes its probe history. Auth always required, plus the typed confirmation phrase DELETE <id> in the JSON body — an unauthenticated delete could take a provider offline.
Adds an API key to a provider's key pool: tests the key live against the upstream, then encrypts and persists it. Auth always required — it plants a credential.
Removes one API key from a provider's key pool (the last key cannot be removed — remove the provider instead). Auth always required — it drops a credential.
Changes one provider key's role (preferred/reserve). Auth always required — it changes which credential routes.

Rotates one provider key's credential in place: tests the replacement key live against the upstream, then replaces the stored ciphertext keeping the key's ID and role. Auth always required — it plants a credential.

Enables or disables a provider: a disabled provider stops routing (the dashboard shows it as Not connected) and re-enabling returns it to the pool with no restart. Auth always required — it changes what routes.
Live provider catalog for the add-provider selector (id, name, verification, ToS-grey flag, base-URL availability) — catalog facts only, no keys, no base URLs.

Cost summary for one gateway key (apiKeyId query param): calendar limits, warning threshold, reset cadence, last/next reset, spend today / this month / this budget period, the active limit and the allow/warn/deny budget check, plus the rolling 5h cap. Management auth (admin scope) required.

Set the calendar budget for one gateway key: daily/weekly/monthly limits, warning threshold, reset interval/time. Absent fields keep their stored values; the 5h cap and unpriced policy are untouched. Ledger-first, then config persist with rollback. Management auth (admin scope) required.
Usage analytics summary for one calendar window: request/token/latency totals, priced spend + cost_status. Management auth (admin scope) required.
Usage analytics roll-up by provider for one calendar window, with priced cost and unpriced-request count. Management auth (admin scope) required.
Usage analytics roll-up by model for one calendar window, with priced cost and unpriced-request count. Management auth (admin scope) required.
Priced spend + unpriced remainder for one calendar window; deliberately no total-cost field. Management auth (admin scope) required.
Compression savings roll-up by provider for one calendar window (prompt tokens before compression, tokens saved, saving rate). Management auth (admin scope) required.
Traffic diversity for one calendar window: provider/model spread with Herfindahl concentration index. Management auth (admin scope) required.
Auto-routed traffic for one calendar window, grouped by variant, with serving providers. Management auth (admin scope) required.

Per-combo health for one calendar window: step liveness from the live provider config plus matching usage requests (upper bound — a row served through a combo is indistinguishable from one served directly). Management auth (admin scope) required.

Fallback chains: every stored (model → provider priority list) chain, or one chain with ?model=. Provider and model names plus priorities only — no keys, no message content. Gateway-key auth required.
Creates or updates one fallback chain (model + ordered provider entries). Management auth (admin scope) required — it rewrites routing state.
Deletes one fallback chain by ?model=; 404 when the model has no chain. Management auth (admin scope) required — it rewrites routing state.
Live resilience feed: breaker states + cooldowns per provider (unknown when unprobed); hedge counts honestly unknown. Management auth (admin scope) required.

Live resilience settings: effective cooldown mode (global + per-model overrides), cooling targets and breaker states from the engine, plus the list of settings with no runtime backing. Management auth (admin scope) required.

Updates resilience settings: cooldown mode (global + per-model overrides) is applied live and persisted; breaker_threshold, breaker_open_for_seconds and cooldown_seconds are validated for range first (400 on a bad range) and then answer 501 naming the field — they have no runtime backing. Management auth (admin scope) required.

Resets one provider's circuit breaker, or all breakers with {"all": true}; unknown provider is 404. A real reset against the production engine — router.Engine implements ResetBreaker/ResetAllBreakers (internal/router/router.go) — 501 only when the engine lacks the breaker-reset interface. Management auth (admin scope) required.
Sets one model's cooldown mode (hard / soft-demote); an empty mode is 400 — clearing an override is DELETE /api/resilience/cooldowns/{model...}. Management auth (admin scope) required.

Clears one model's cooldown-mode override so it inherits the global mode again; idempotent — a model with no override still answers 200. The model id uses the multi-segment wildcard because model ids contain a slash. Management auth (admin scope) required.
Recent server log lines, double-redacted, newest first (?limit, default 50, max 500); captured:false with an empty list until log capture is wired. Management auth (admin scope) required.
Dry-run probe of the local guardrails against sample text: findings + would-block verdict; records nothing, sends nothing upstream. Management auth (admin scope) required.
List team cost centers with live budget/member/consumption views. Management auth (admin scope) required.
Create a team cost center (name, budget, duration, members). Management auth (admin scope) required.
One team cost center by id; unknown ids answer 404. Management auth (admin scope) required.
Update one team cost center (budget, members, status). Management auth (admin scope) required.
Delete one team cost center. Management auth (admin scope) required.
List fair-share quota pools with live pool-wide consumption. Management auth (admin scope) required.
Create a fair-share quota pool (dimensions, allocations, saturation threshold). Management auth (admin scope) required.
One fair-share quota pool by id; unknown ids answer 404. Management auth (admin scope) required.
Update one fair-share quota pool (dimensions, allocations). Management auth (admin scope) required.
Delete one fair-share quota pool. Management auth (admin scope) required.

Registers a webhook URL + event list (quota.exceeded, budget.warning): validates the URL (http/https only, no private/loopback targets), mints a wh_ id, persists to the config file and rebuilds the live dispatcher. Auth always required — it points the server at an operator-chosen URL and stores a signing secret.
Lists webhook registrations (id, url, events, has_secret only — secrets never returned). Management auth (admin scope) required.
One webhook registration by id (secret never returned); unknown id is 404. Management auth (admin scope) required.
Removes a webhook registration, persists the config file and rebuilds the live dispatcher; unknown id is 404. Auth always required — it silently drops an operator alert channel.

Updates a webhook registration (partial update: url, events and secret are each optional, only provided fields change; the URL is re-validated when changed). Persists to the config file and rebuilds the live dispatcher; unknown id is 404. Auth always required — it can re-point an operator alert channel.

Terminal-friendly usage command for the calling gateway key (@@om-usage): spend today / this week / this month, the active limit and next reset — plain text by default, JSON with ?format=json. Only for keys the operator enabled allow_usage_command on (403 otherwise). Gateway-key auth required.

Live cache analytics — per-layer entries/bytes/hits/misses/hit-ratio for the exact + semantic caches, totals, single-flight coalescing counters, and aggregated savings (tokens + USD) when a savings recorder is wired; savings omitted with a note when not. Counts only, no keys, no message content.

Per-(provider, model) measured latency percentiles p50/p95/p99 from recorded request samples, with sample counts; optional ?provider= / ?model= exact-match filters. Read-only counts and latencies, no keys, no message content.
Operator price book: per-(provider, model) rates with their source (ledger, book, synced, model fallback). Read-only, rates and sources only, no secrets.
Replaces price-book rates for (provider, model) pairs (all-or-nothing, validated, persisted to the config file with rollback). Auth always required — it changes what every request is charged.
Flushes every cache layer (exact, semantic, reasoning) and reports per-layer evicted counts. Auth always required — it discards cached answers.
Prometheus exposition — gateway-key auth required.
Model list — gateway-key auth required.
Model list filtered by provider and free-tier-only; capability filter answers 400 — the catalog records no per-model capability flags. Gateway-key auth required.
Per-model health from the health-probe ring — each model's status is its provider's last probe result; unprobed models report unknown. Gateway-key auth required.
Single model detail — catalog entry for one model (price, base-URL presence, free-tier flag); unknown models answer 404. Gateway-key auth required.
Chat completions pinned to one provider — gateway-key auth required.
Model list for one provider — gateway-key auth required.
Status for one provider (configured, key count, breaker, cooling) — gateway-key auth required.
Gemini-native model list — gateway-key auth required.
Gemini-native generateContent / streamGenerateContent — gateway-key auth required.
Chat completions — gateway-key auth required.

A2A JSON-RPC endpoint (message/send, message/stream, tasks/get, tasks/cancel + v1.0 SendMessage/SendStreamingMessage aliases) — gateway-key auth required, owner-scoped to the caller's key; disabled unless config a2a_enabled is true.

A2A operator status: enabled flag, live per-state task counts (operator-only aggregates across all owners), the six skill ids and the protocol version. Management auth (admin scope) required; while A2A is disabled it answers enabled:false with all-zero counts and never touches the store.

A2A agent card (discovery document for the POST /a2a task interface): name, description, url, version, input/output modes, capabilities and the six skill descriptors — public, no auth; no task data, no keys, no provider details.

Embeddings — OpenAI-compatible, routed through the same engine as chat completions (budgets, guardrails, ledger, route trace) but replay-exempt: exactly one upstream attempt, never replayed onto another target. Gateway-key auth required.
Multimodal embeddings (text + image/media inputs) — routed through the engine, replay-exempt. Gateway-key auth required.

Rerank — Cohere/LiteLLM shape (model, query, documents, top_n, return_documents), routed through the same engine as chat completions but replay-exempt: exactly one upstream attempt, never replayed onto another target. Gateway-key auth required.
Legacy completions — gateway-key auth required.
Chat completions explicitly routed with context-relay strategy. Gateway-key auth required.
Routing classification — gateway-key auth required.
Routing explanation — gateway-key auth required.
Prompt segmentation + classification — gateway-key auth required.

Images generations — OpenAI-compatible, routed through the same engine as chat completions (budgets, guardrails, ledger, route trace) but replay-exempt: exactly one upstream attempt, never replayed onto another target. Gateway-key auth required.

Images edits — OpenAI-compatible multipart/form-data, forwarded verbatim (never decoded and rebuilt), routed through the same engine as chat completions but replay-exempt: exactly one upstream attempt, never replayed onto another target. Gateway-key auth required.

Audio speech (text-to-speech) — OpenAI-compatible, routed through the same engine as chat completions but replay-exempt: exactly one upstream attempt, never replayed onto another target. Gateway-key auth required.
Alias of POST /v1/audio/speech — not an OpenAI endpoint; gateway route name, same handler and operation. Gateway-key auth required.

Text-to-speech with the voice id in the URL path: the id is written into the JSON body's voice field (a conflicting body voice is refused 400), then the request follows POST /v1/audio/speech. Gateway-key auth required.
Audio transcriptions (speech-to-text) — OpenAI-compatible multipart upload, replay-exempt: exactly one upstream attempt. Gateway-key auth required.
Alias of POST /v1/audio/transcriptions — not an OpenAI endpoint; gateway route name, same handler and operation. Gateway-key auth required.
Audio translations (translate audio to English) — OpenAI-compatible multipart upload, replay-exempt: exactly one upstream attempt. Gateway-key auth required.

Moderations — OpenAI-shaped, backed ONLY by the router's local guardrails (PII / secret / injection patterns); no upstream call, no input stored or echoed. The 13 OpenAI categories are not judged (all false, score 0); the real verdict is in results[].local_guardrails and results[].flagged reflects it. Gateway-key auth required.
Search — Perplexity Search API passthrough, verbatim, replay-exempt: exactly one upstream attempt, never replayed onto another target. Gateway-key auth required.
Fetches and extracts clean text from a web URL with SSRF protection. Gateway-key auth required.
OCR — Mistral OCR API passthrough, verbatim, replay-exempt: exactly one upstream attempt. Gateway-key auth required.
Video generations — Runway text-to-video passthrough, returns a task id; replay-exempt: exactly one upstream attempt. Gateway-key auth required.
Video task status — Runway task poll by id; unknown ids answer 404. Gateway-key auth required.
Music generations — MiniMax music generation passthrough, synchronous; replay-exempt: exactly one upstream attempt. Gateway-key auth required.

Anthropic Messages dialect — byte-for-byte native relay to a Messages provider (only the model field rewritten; cache_control and the SSE envelope pass through untouched), translate path through the engine when a feature needs the canonical form. Gateway-key auth required.
Token count for a Messages request body — counted locally, never sent upstream. Gateway-key auth required.

OpenAI Responses API — translated to the canonical chat request and routed through the same engine as chat completions (failover, budgets, guardrails, ledger); creates fail over pre-commit, including branched continuations, which replay the same branched input against the next target (the original provider is tried first). Gateway-key auth required.

Retrieve one served Responses object by gateway response id — the stored object, byte-identical to what the create served, plus child_response_ids (the branches off it, from the ledger tree); unknown ids answer 404. Gateway-key auth required.

List served Responses objects, newest first, paginated (limit + after cursor) — the full stored objects, byte-identical to what each create served; an unknown cursor is a 400. Gateway-key auth required.
Deletes one stored response (transcript + served object) so continuations of it answer 404; deleting an unknown id is an honest 404, never a silent success. Gateway-key auth required.
Input items of one stored Responses object, paginated (limit + after cursor, asc/desc); unknown ids answer 404. Gateway-key auth required.
Token count for a stored response's input — counted locally, never sent upstream. Gateway-key auth required.
Upload a file (multipart form-data: file + purpose) to the local disk store; returns the OpenAI-shaped file object.
List stored files, newest first.
Retrieve one stored file's metadata by id; unknown ids answer 404.
Delete one stored file (content + index entry); unknown ids answer 404, never a silent success.
Download one stored file's bytes; unknown ids answer 404.
Create a batch from an input file id (endpoint must be /v1/chat/completions, completion_window must be 24h); returns the Batch object in status validating.
List the caller's batches, newest first (?limit= default 20, max 100).
Retrieve one batch by id; unknown or foreign ids answer 404.
Cancel a running batch: cancelling -> cancelled, the worker stops starting new lines; already-terminal batches answer 409.
Delete one terminal batch record; non-terminal batches answer 409, unknown or foreign ids answer 404.
Delete all of the caller's terminal (completed/cancelled/failed/expired) batch records; in-progress batches are never deleted.

Authenticated gateway-key introspection: the caller's key id/fingerprint, created/expiry, spend this period, budget remaining, traffic limits and live usage — never the key value itself. Gateway-key auth required; an expired key answers 401 naming the expiry.

List agent sessions opened by the calling API key: Responses chains (one row per session root, no previous_response_id, with turns, cumulative tokens and the list-price cost of its requests) plus ledger agent sessions (one row per coding-agent session, with request/error counts, token split and record-time cost). unpricedCount counts turns/requests with no known catalog price. Every row is filtered to the calling key — other keys' sessions are never listed. Gateway-key auth required.

One agent session of the calling API key: a Responses session (the session root's turns, cumulative tokens and list-price cost, plus the per-turn detail) or a ledger agent session (request/error counts, token split, record-time cost, no per-turn detail); unknown ids, other keys' sessions and keyless records answer 404. Gateway-key auth required.

Pre-flight quota/budget check for one (provider, model, estimated tokens) request: allowed plus the budget, token-limit and price numbers the verdict was judged against, from the same ledger machinery that enforces live requests. Gateway-key auth required.

Auto-combo candidate pool for one auto/* channel: live tier models with per-key connections and breaker/cooldown state — a read-only transparency listing, never a dispatch preview. Gateway-key auth required.
List named routing combos (chains): one row per combo with steps, strategy and usability. Gateway-key auth required.
Create a named routing combo (ordered provider/model steps + strategy), mirrored into the routing groups so it routes immediately. Management auth (admin scope) required — it rewrites routing state.
One named routing combo by id; unknown ids answer 404. Gateway-key auth required.
Update one named routing combo (chain, strategy, rename). Management auth (admin scope) required — it rewrites routing state.
Delete one named routing combo (record + group mirror + strategy mirror). Management auth (admin scope) required — it rewrites routing state.

Imports named routing combos from an export file (one at a time); imported combos are mirrored into routing groups like created ones. Management auth (admin scope) required — it rewrites routing state.
Exports all named routing combos in the importable shape. Gateway-key auth required.
Exports one named routing combo in the importable shape; unknown ids answer 404. Gateway-key auth required.
Duplicates one named routing combo under a new id (disabled copies stay unmirrored). Management auth (admin scope) required — it rewrites routing state.
Simulates one combo run step by step (provider key presence per step); never calls upstream, never spends quota. Gateway-key auth required.
Enables one named routing combo and re-mirrors its stored chain + strategy. Management auth (admin scope) required — it rewrites routing state.
Disables one named routing combo (unmirrors it from routing). Management auth (admin scope) required — it rewrites routing state.
Terminates the server process.

Graceful restart: answers 202, stops the HTTP server, flushes caches, then starts a replacement process (under the tray supervisor: exits with the restart code and the supervisor relaunches the gateway; unsupervised: re-launches the same binary with the same arguments). 503 when the process has no restart hook.
Unavailable: answers 501 feature_unavailable, does nothing (system service installation is not supported in this build). Use instead: `codvian-router restart` starts a supervised background gateway.
Unavailable: answers 501 feature_unavailable, does nothing (dynamic plugin loading is unsupported by design: plugins are compiled-in and enabled from config at startup (docs/plugins.md)).

Update check: asks the GitHub releases API for the latest release and answers {current, latest, release_available, update_available, release_url}. When the repository exists but has no published release it answers 200 with latest null, release_available false and status no_published_release (no tag or URL invented). Failures carry their kind in error.code: 503 rate_limited (with Retry-After), 504 timeout, 502 for network, auth, upstream 5xx, malformed response or repository not found. It never downloads or installs anything; installing is `codvian-router update` (signature + checksum verified). 503 when no update checker is wired.
Starts the local TCP tunnel: forwards a loopback port to the gateway's listen address (real TCP proxy, loopback-only, stdlib only).
Stops the running local TCP tunnel and reports the bytes it forwarded.
Live tunnel status (running/stopped, ports, bytes forwarded) — loopback-only like the other tunnel routes.
Unavailable: answers 501 feature_unavailable, does nothing (provider sign-in (OAuth / device-code login) is not supported in this build). Use instead: POST /api/providers with an API key.
Fresh-install first-key setup — only while no gateway key exists; claims with the one-shot bootstrap token printed to stdout at first boot (loopback-only).

Exports the full settings snapshot. Secrets are redacted and never exported — provider keys and gateway-key hashes stay on disk. Requires gateway-key auth AND the typed confirmation phrase EXPORT SETTINGS (the operator-credential second check).

Exports the config + ledger usage history as a downloadable JSON file. All secrets redacted (no provider keys, no gateway-key hashes, no base URLs); usage history is read-only, never reset. Requires gateway-key auth AND the typed confirmation phrase EXPORT.

Issues a single-use DB-wipe confirmation token (5-minute TTL, stored hashed, never logged). Requires gateway-key auth AND the typed confirmation phrase WIPE DATABASE — the token is the operator-credential second check for the wipe.

Irreversibly wipes usage history: ledger usage events, budget running spend, feedback decisions/signals, probe history (ring + file + backup). Providers, provider keys, gateway keys, prices and all other config are preserved. Requires gateway-key auth AND the typed phrase WIPE DATABASE AND the single-use confirmation token from /admin/db/wipe/arm — a key alone, or a key plus phrase, cannot wipe.

Imports a DB export file (codvian-router-db-export/v1) and merges its usage history into the ledger — never resets or wipes existing history; duplicate events are skipped, never double-counted; the file's config section is ignored. Requires gateway-key auth AND the typed confirmation phrase IMPORT.

Revokes every gateway key (including the caller's) and persists the empty key list; bootstrap becomes pending so a new first key can be issued loopback-only. Requires the typed confirmation phrase REVOKE ALL.

Updates one gateway key's expiry and per-key traffic limits (requests-per-minute, tokens-per-minute) and persists the change. Auth always required — it changes which credential can authenticate and how much traffic it may send.

Regenerates one gateway key: the old key is revoked at rotation and a new key is issued in its place (same name/scopes/budget/limits unless overridden), returned exactly once and never logged. Auth always required — it revokes a credential and mints a new one.
Mints one new gateway key via config.IssueKey and persists it; the raw key is returned once in the response and never logged. Auth always required — it creates a credential.

Registers one OAuth 2.0 client (PKCE public or confidential) for gateway auth; a confidential client's secret is returned once in the response and never logged. Auth always required — it creates a credential.
Lists registered OAuth clients (no secrets). Auth always required.
Deletes one OAuth client and revokes its outstanding codes and refresh tokens. Auth always required — it destroys a credential.

OAuth 2.0 authorization endpoint (code + PKCE S256): the operator's gateway key approves the grant; the granted scopes must be a subset of the operator key's scopes. Issues a single-use code by 302 redirect to the client's registered redirect_uri. Auth always required — it mints a credential.
Stores an externally-issued key definition under its hash; the raw key is never logged and never returned. Auth always required — it installs a credential.

Permanently revokes one gateway key: removes it from the config (persisted) so it stops authenticating at once; the reversible kill-switch is POST /admin/keys/{id} with {"disabled":true}. Auth always required — it destroys a credential, plus the typed confirmation phrase DELETE <id>.

Resets the config to defaults (providers, gateway keys, budget, routing, guardrails, auto-router) and persists it; listen address, data dir and unknown fields are preserved, usage history is not wiped. Requires the typed confirmation phrase RESET CONFIG.
Flushes the gateway exact-match cache: an empty body flushes every entry; {"key_id"} flushes only that gateway key's entries. Auth always required — it discards cached answers.
Live server status (uptime, provider count, guard state) — gateway-key auth required.

OAuth 2.0 token endpoint: authorization_code (PKCE) and refresh_token grants; issues HS256 JWT access tokens (1h) + rotating refresh tokens (30d). No gateway key — client authentication is the code_verifier and the client secret.
OAuth 2.0 revocation endpoint (RFC 7009): revokes a refresh token or a JWT access token; always answers 200, even for a token that was never issued. No gateway key.
Built-in gateway-key templates (names, scopes, budgets); secret-free by construction — a template holds no key material. Gateway-key auth required.
